# Sage migration (Phase D)

Moves a Sage Business Cloud Accounting (SA, API v2) export into ONE company: categories -> items -> purchase orders, through
the MCP write tools (`upsert_item_category`, `bulk_upsert_items`, `bulk_create_purchase_orders`) and their real registry.
Assumed export shape and field mapping: `docs/design/sage-migration-export-format.md`. CLI: `scripts/sage-migration/run.ts`.
Local throwaway databases only.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `sageExportTypes.ts` / `sageValues.ts` | Typed rows, `RowRefusal`, `ParsedExport`; the field readers (every fault of a row is collected, not the first). |
| `sageItemParser.ts` / `sagePurchaseOrderParser.ts` / `sageExportParser.ts` | PURE. Row parsers, then the file-level checks (duplicate id / code / number refuse every row sharing it; category conflicts; unknown status; a PO line naming an item the export lacks). |
| `sageTaxTypes.ts` / `sagePoStatus.ts` | The two assumed tables: tax type 1 standard, 2 zero, 3 exempt; Pending/Overdue -> open, Invoiced -> billed (closed), Cancelled. Anything else is refused, never guessed. |
| `sageItemMapping.ts` / `sagePurchaseOrderMapping.ts` | PURE mapping to the tools' arguments (the table is in each header). |
| `sageSuppliers.ts` | Supplier by Sage reference (`find_by_external_ref`), else exact name (`list_suppliers`); none or two is a refusal of the PO. |
| `sageMigrationPlan.ts` | PURE. What is sent and what is refused first: each row goes through the tool's own pure validator (`validateItemFields`, `parsePurchaseOrder`) and against what the company already holds (`sageSnapshot.ts`: a code another item carries, a deleted item, a taken PO number), so one bad row costs that row, not its batch. A PO line naming a refused item goes unlinked (suffix kept, counted); the PO is refused only when the item is not in the export (`line_item_unknown`) or is refused with no readable Code (`line_item_refused`). |
| `sageBatches.ts` / `sageBatchRun.ts` | Batches (items 500, POs 100: the tools' own caps, pinned equal by a test), stable order, deterministic keys `sage-mig-<entity>-<n>-<hash of the rows>`, plus the state salt (`stateSalt`: a hash of the existing rows a batch touches) and the `--run-tag` when given, so a key is `sage-mig-<entity>-<n>-<hash>` with the salt and tag folded into the hash; the one call that sends a batch. |
| `sageToolSession.ts` | One request transaction as `app_user` with the member's claims, the real `mcpRegistry.call`; `commit: false` rolls the lot back. What keeps a run inside its company is NOT the `company_id` argument sent on writes (the registry only compares it with the context's own company: it selects nothing): it is the membership check (the user must be an active member of the named company), `app_user` under RLS with that company's claims, and the tools' own ownership checks. |
| `sageMigrationRunner.ts` | Dry run, then live; `sageSnapshot.ts` + `sageReconciliation.ts` + `sageReportSummary.ts` measure and print the result. |
| `sageRunLock.ts` | One run per company: a session advisory lock on its own connection for the whole run; the connection is watched (`check()` before the live phase and between phases, `LockLostError` -> `MigrationStopped` "lock lost", exit 4). |
| `sagePoContent.ts` | PURE. THE column lists (compared / excluded with a reason) of `purchase_orders` and `po_items`, `storedPoFrom` (the row set the PO tool would write for the plan's element) and the generic compare with the books' whole rows; checked against information_schema and the tool's INSERTs by `sage-migration-po-columns.int.test.ts`. A new column is decided there, never skipped. |
| `sageOwnership.ts` / `sageDifferences.ts` | What the migration owns (system exactly `sage`, this ref) and the checks that the books hold what a batch sent; the PO / item / category differences list, deduped. |
| `sageLineLinks.ts` / `sageAccountCheck.ts` / `sageBudgetReport.ts` | PO lines not linked to an item (informational), the `--po-gl-account` check, and the budget findings of the dry run. |
| `sageMigrationTypes.ts` / `sageMigrationStopped.ts` / `sageStopMessage.ts` | Report and option types; the error after the live phase started (with what was committed); the CLI message and its exit code (`exitCodeForError`: 2 nothing written, 4 stopped after live started). |
| `sageRowWording.ts` / `sageVerify.ts` | PURE. THE wording of what a live batch did to an owned row (summary and stop alike: from the batch's LIVE answer); the phases' checks against the books (`verified*`: rows absent, rows other than sent -> `changedAfterCommit` + `changedRows`) and what a stop is handed. |
| `localGuard.ts` | The runner starts only on a local throwaway database (127.0.0.1/localhost, explicit port outside 7770-7776, db `isaflow_schema_fixture` / `isaflow_test` / `isaflow_sagemig_*`), for DATABASE_URL and every other database URL set. |

## Rules

- `--live` is not started (`live_blocked`, exit 1, nothing written) on a dry run that misses `--expect-*` (against what would be SENT), refuses rows without `--allow-refusals`, or differs without `--allow-differences`. The dry run's item outcomes are checked against the snapshot (a writer landing between them fails the dry run); the window dry run -> live is a named limit.
- Text with a NUL byte or a lone surrogate is refused per row (`invalid_text`); pages must be whole (`$startIndex` where the rows before end, no `$back` on the first); `external_system` of items and categories is compared exactly; an owned item with stock movements is never flipped (`item_has_stock_movements`); a PO of an inactive supplier is `supplier_inactive`; `--po-gl-account` must be an active, non-header expense account; a summary is printed before `--report` is written (exit 3 if it fails).

- **The migration only updates items it owns.** `bulk_upsert_items` matches by code and updates what it matches, so a Sage code equal to any other item (no reference, another reference, deleted) is refused `code_held_by_existing_item` in the plan and the item named.
- A supplier carrying another Sage reference is never matched by name. A PO in a foreign currency, or with a description that would pass 500 with its item suffix, is refused.
- A partial export (no container, unknown top-level key, `$totalResults` other than the rows read across ALL pages, `$next` on the LAST (or only) page (Sage keeps it on every other page), an unknown `$`-key on a page, a row that is an array or carries a page marker) is refused whole; `--live` needs `--expect-items` and `--expect-pos`.
- A replayed batch whose rows are gone is `replayed, rows absent` (failed); `--run-tag` salts the keys for a deliberate fresh import.
- Pending/Overdue go in through one constant, `OPEN_SAGE_PO_IMPORTED_AS`.

- **`QuantityOnHand` is NEVER imported** (Hein). It is not on the typed row at all (the export parser only counts the rows carrying it, any spelling), not on any mapped row, and
  no `stock_movements`, `opening_qty` or `current_qty` is written; the report counts the movements before and after.
- `inventory_tracked` is always false; a Sage service code (`Physical` false) is a service.
- The dry run is one rolled-back transaction. Categories and purchase orders are written LIVE inside it (items' preview needs the
  categories; PO batch k's budget check must see batches 1..k-1, as the live run's does); items are written live too (the same code and constraints). Its idempotency and audit
  rows roll back with it (a test proves it). A dry run that is not clean stops the run: nothing is written, even with `live`.
- Two live suppliers carrying one Sage reference refuse the POs (`supplier_ambiguous`). The lock is asked before EVERY live batch (`check()`: the error flag plus one bounded `SELECT 1`; `unlock` is bounded too). Before a live run `--expect-po-total` is compared with the PROJECTED booked total. `Lines[].LineType` is optional and ASSUMED (0 item, 1 account; unconfirmed, open question in the design doc): 1 refuses the PO (`po_account_line_unsupported`), any other value (`po_line_type_unknown`); a non-item line is never linked. The coding columns of a line (gl_account_id, cc1_id, cc2_id, bu_id) are EXCLUDED from the re-run compare (IsaFlow-owned).
- A booked PO whose Sage supplier no longer resolves is sent under its booked supplier and LISTED as a supplier difference (never refused, never adopted as the resolution); booked to a deleted supplier it is refused (`booked_supplier_deleted`). A PO ref held by two POs is refused (`po_ref_ambiguous`). A non-JSON success from a tool fails the batch (in a live request it throws, so the request rolls back: "failed, nothing written" is true). A live batch whose COMMIT does not answer STOPS the run there, in any phase (`MigrationStopped`, exit 4, listed `commit unconfirmed`): no later batch is checked against books that may not hold it.
- "Already booked" is by Sage REFERENCE (the tool replays by it): a renumbered booked PO is sent, its number a difference, keyed by the number the books hold. One Sage supplier id under two names matching two IsaFlow suppliers refuses its POs. A stop checks its "committed" batches against the books (replayed rows absent are named, with `--run-tag`). `notes` is not compared (named limit).
- `runSageMigration` itself refuses `live` without `expect.items` and `expect.purchaseOrders` (opt-out: `liveWithoutCounts: true`, for TESTS and programmatic callers ONLY: the CLI never sets it: `sageCliOptions.test.ts` runs `run.ts` with `--live` and both counts against a mocked runner and reads the options back (no `liveWithoutCounts`); the CLI suite's F4 checks `--live` without the counts is exit 2, nothing written (run.ts refuses before the runner); a person always gives `--expect-items` and `--expect-pos`). A phase that never started is `skipped` ("not run"); every live phase's batches are rows-present-checked; COMMIT is bounded (`COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS` = `SAGE_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS` 70 s, a timeout is `commitUnconfirmed`).
- A container that mixes pages and plain rows is a `SageExportShapeError`. 0 or "" in ItemId / SelectionId / TaxTypeId* / Category.ID, and a `{}` or blank-Description Category, are refused with "unknown whether Sage means none" (`readId(..., mayMeanNone)`, fail closed, open question in the design doc); a row's own ID 0 or SupplierId 0 is a plain bad id. **Wording rule (round 12):** every was / may have been / would be / nothing-written claim, in the summary and the stop, comes from the LIVE tool answer of the batch that carried the row (`sageRowWording.ts`), never the dry run's while a live one exists; "replayed / nothing written" only when the registry SAID it served a stored answer (`ctx.onIdempotentReplay` -> `replayed`) or the request rolled back; the books check only adds "then changed in the books since" to the rows it named (`changedRows`; the others "another row of its batch changed since"). An unconfirmed COMMIT keeps its live answer (`CommitUnconfirmedError.result`). A stopped CLI run writes a stop report to `--report`. A field the parsers read spelled any other way (keys compared normalised by `fieldKey`, Category's too) refuses the row (`recasedFieldReasons`), and `LineType ""` is `po_line_type_unknown`; a discount (a key holding disc / markdown / allowance / percentoff / rebate) that is not zero refuses the row (`po_discount_unsupported` / `item_discount_unsupported`, `sageMoneyFields.ts`), so does any other unread money-like PO / line key that is not zero (`po_money_field_unsupported`; the first real export decides the reviewed list, no override flag); `sageLineMoney.ts`: a line Tax / Total without Exclusive is refused, Total is Exclusive + Tax (or + the tool's own tax at the rate), UnitPriceInclusive / SubTotal / AmountDue (open POs only) are read and refuse only when they disagree, UnitPriceInclusive with no line Tax also against what is booked; an `Inclusive` true PO needs every line's own Exclusive and Tax (B14-1, refused rather than guessed); a negative id is refused; a batch that wrote nothing stays "nothing new written" when a row changes after it, and a stop report lists batches by outcome (`batchOutcome`); `--report` (`scripts/sage-migration/runReport.ts`, rounds 16-17): the path must NOT exist; the run creates it exclusively ("running") after every check that needs no database (the export read too) and before the first database step, then writes ONLY through that held descriptor (truncate + write at 0 + fsync; no temp, no rename), a stop report on every exit after the create, nothing before it; a failed final write leaves `report_not_written`, a failed stop report `stop_report_not_written`; SIGINT / SIGTERM / SIGHUP stop the run before its next batch, dry or live, never after the last (`MigrationOptions.shouldStop`; dry exit 2, live exit 4 and a stop report); a second signal, an uncaught error or an unhandled rejection ends it at once through one `terminate` whose stop report comes from `MigrationOptions.onProgress` (`scripts/sage-migration/runState.ts`; exit 4 only once live started); EPIPE on stdout/stderr never ends a run; withToolSession listens to the client's `error` while checked out; a loss before a live batch's COMMIT is sent is `LostBeforeCommitError` (round-22 rule: no COMMIT was sent, the batch FAILED, nothing written, the run stops exit 4), a loss at the COMMIT (57P01-03, pg's own "Connection terminated", the client's error) is `CommitUnconfirmedError.connectionLost` keeping the live answer (a refusal stays a refusal), a loss in a request that commits nothing (the dry run, which writes and rolls back, the plan, a read) is `ConnectionLostError` (the server rolled it back; pre-live exit 2); a stop never uses the dry run's answer for a live batch; a dry run whose ROLLBACK is not confirmed (not a loss) refuses a live start (`DryRollbackUnconfirmedError`, its backend pid said, exit 2; `withToolSession(..., { wrote: true })`) and otherwise keeps its result with `dryRunHeld` (a WARNING line: a preview, a failed or blocked dry run), the plan and plain reads keep what they read; every request sets `lock_timeout` (10 s) and `statement_timeout` (60 s), and the CLI's pool keepalive + `query_timeout` (75 s) + `connectionTimeoutMillis` (15 s; `sageTimeouts.ts`, `sagePoolConfig`; the COMMIT bound 70 s sits between statement and query timeouts): a "Query read timeout" is a loss (later queries fail at once; in the dry run with an unconfirmed ROLLBACK it is held writes), a connect that fails sent nothing, a 57014 is `StatementTimeoutError` by SQLSTATE only (worded by how long it ran: past the statement_timeout, or cancelled sooner by another session; the session's own cancel at its ROLLBACK is not one) and a stall recorded by the request wins over the error it caused wherever it was raised (`stallFirst`: session.call and the request's catch; the dry run stops at that batch, live exit 4); ending a holder is offered only for a migration transaction left open (`sageLockHolder.ts` `ownLeftOpen`: this company's `sageAppName` (`ours`), idle in a transaction in two samples `HOLDER_CONFIRM_MS` apart with state_change unchanged, older than the run lock `MigrationOptions.runLockAt`; "its client may be gone"); the idle-transaction default is the holder's own (pg_db_role_setting), said as a default; BLOCKER_SQL is a UNION on pid to the root, flags `waiting` and `cycle` (never "at work"); read through the pool; a failed key-holder lookup is logged, "could not be read"; a held live key never claims an unconfirmed COMMIT ("had not received a COMMIT when looked up"); a COMMIT the server answered with an ERROR is `CommitRefusedError` (rolled back, nothing written, the run stops), only no answer is unconfirmed; a live read-timeout loss names its pid; run.ts ends a run in one act (`scripts/sage-migration/runEnd.ts`: RunState.ended set before any wait; then shouldStop stops, sessions refuse with `RunEndedError` via `MigrationOptions.ended`, main does nothing more; a crash waits, bounded (80 s), for the in-flight batch and says and writes its outcome, a first signal then says what it waits for, a second exits at once; a failed rewrite never empties the report, and its lines say which body the file holds) and says every line through `runConsole.ts` (its queues in `runConsoleQueue.ts`: a queue and a no-progress budget per stream, one when 2>&1; a stream given up is said on the other, naming only where --report is; what it holds is the one final word at every end, `OwnedReport.finalWord` after its last write, on a stream still alive; every exit waits for it, at most 120 s from the first ask, a second signal exits at once; O_NONBLOCK set again before every pipe write, the exit's one tries included) and ends its pool last and bounded; the session watches its queries through a Proxy view of its client (never patching it; `sageWaitWatch.ts` says a 5 s wait and who blocks it via `onNotice`, samples tagged by wait so a late one is never kept for the next, the run lock's connect watched too), a 55P03 stops the dry run at the first batch (`LockWaitError`, holder pid; --live exit 2, preview exit 1) and a live batch (exit 4); a write tool's idempotency key is taken without waiting (`sageKeyLock.ts`: the registry's text, trimmed and per-user; `BatchKeyHeldError` names the holder, worded by phase); RunInProgressError names the run lock's holder, an unconfirmed release is a WARNING; the session's errors live in `sageSessionErrors.ts`; named limit (R23-4): a backend dying with no ErrorResponse whose FIN comes after the final answer leaves the loss unseen, so the COMMIT is sent into the dying socket (commit unconfirmed, the safe side) and a failed answer that was the loss reads "the tool refused"; pre-live exit 2); SIGHUP defeats nohup and an exit-4 summary is stderr-only (named limits); the per-unit UnitPriceInclusive check takes 1 cent either way, the booked gross stays exact; isZeroish takes `0%` / `0,00`; every QuantityOnHand row is counted; a PO batch with `created` > 0 or the counter raised wrote something; a stop re-checks committed batches like the live phases (`settleCommitted`); a refused CLI start writes the stop report too; a dry run `would be`, and its report has `bookedTotalCents` / `differenceCents` null.
- A valid row sharing an ID/Code/DocumentNumber with an INVALID row is refused too (`duplicate_*`). A pool under 2 connections is refused at the start (the run lock holds one); the lock session sets `idle_session_timeout` to 0 and is pinged every 15 s.
- A PO already booked by this migration is never refused on a re-run for an inactive supplier or the block policy (both are for new POs). A lock lost BEFORE the live phase starts (the check after the dry run) is exit 2, nothing written; the check before the first live batch, and every later one, is exit 4 (the live phase has started). A batch whose COMMIT failed is `commitUnconfirmed` and listed as such.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 not ok, 2 refused/failed to start (nothing written), 3 report not written, 4 stopped after the live phase started (batches may be committed). Every tool the runner calls is free in `flowMetering`: a PAYG wallet is untouched by a dry or live run.
- Exit 0 needs a clean dry run or a live run that booked everything it sent, `--expect-*` figures that match what was SENT (dry) or
  BOOKED (live), and no refused row unless `--allow-refusals`.
- Item codes and PO numbers are unique case-sensitively (plain unique indexes), so the checks against what the company holds are exact.
- A PO line is "No budget" (not judged) unless the run is given `--po-gl-account`. Under the company's `block` policy an approved PO with an account-less line is refused by the PO tool for the WHOLE batch, so the plan refuses each such PO itself (`accountless_under_block_policy`) with the remedies (`--skip-budget-check`, `--po-gl-account`, draft import). `--po-gl-account` which posts EVERY line to that one account: the budget figures are then only as right as that choice. Opt-in only.
- Named limits: what the company holds is read once before the dry run; a writer racing in between can still make a tool refuse a batch (the dry run reports it, writes nothing). A really over-budget PO under `block`, or a supplier merged or deleted after the snapshot, also fails a PO batch whole. An array of pages must show one chain (`$next` on every page but the last, `$totalResults` or `$startIndex` on every page, full pages but the last, `$next` positions matching); `--expect-items` / `--expect-pos` stay the last guard. The normalised key check fails closed also on harmless spellings (`Id`, `SupplierID`, `quantityonhand` refuse the row).
- Every batch key (category, item, PO) carries ONE shared salt (`stateSalt`): a hash of the state of the existing rows the batch touches, so a stored answer is never replayed for a state it was not given for (a PO's: the fields the PO tool compares, its line items, updated_at). One run per company at a time: a session advisory lock (`sageRunLock`), a second run is refused at its start; after the categories and the items phases the books are checked against what was sent before the next phase starts; item codes are compared trimmed.
- A re-run sets owned items and categories back to the values the migration SENDS (IsaFlow edits to those fields are overwritten; the tools never clear a field, so a value Sage dropped stays, unlisted). A PO found already there is never changed; differences (and items that would change) are reported and exit 1 unless `--allow-differences`.
- Two Sage suppliers that resolve by name to one IsaFlow supplier are both refused (`supplier_collapsed`).
- A live batch is one committed registry call. A failed batch is reported with the tool's message and nothing of it is written;
  the other batches of its phase run, the next phase does not. Running again resumes: batches whose rows are absent retry under their own key, the others are fresh calls that answer `unchanged` / already there.
- PO lines link to their item (the PO tool refuses a WHOLE batch for an unknown or inactive item): by `item_code` for an item this run sends and that is active, by `item_id` for an owned item already in the books that is active and not sent this run (never by its stored code: it can carry whitespace the PO tool trims). Any other line goes without it, keeps " [item CODE]" and is counted "line not linked: item inactive/refused"; it cannot cost its batch. A PO found already there is never changed: new links show as differences.
- PDFs are listed in the report, not uploaded.
- The reconciliation is measured in the database (before and after), never taken from a tool's answer.
